The call was malformed. I'll write the script with `write_file` instead.

I wrote `/app/bin/fees.py` and ran it on `/app/data`, saving the result as `/app/out/statements.json`. All 4 unit tests pass, and `python tools/check_fees.py` reports 228 of 228 statements and 4 of 4 branch rows matching the approved ones.

The script follows the rules in `/app/docs` and uses only the standard library. Where the docs left something open, I made these choices:
- **Case and spacing:** I compare branch ids, item types and category names without regard to case, and I strip whitespace from event fields.
- **File names:** Only export files ending in lowercase `.csv` or `.jsonl` are read.
- **Statement fields:** Each statement uses the patron number as `patrons.csv` writes it for the category in force on `period_end`. Item types and categories use the names from `policy.ini`.

I did not test any input beyond the four fixtures and `/app/data`.

I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | head -100; cat docs/overview.md

cd /app/data; cat policy.ini branches.csv; head -20 calendar.csv; head -8 patrons.csv waivers.csv; cat exports/manifest.txt; cd exports; head -4 har-2026-12-28.csv wst-2027-01-22.jsonl resend-cen.csv; ls | grep -v -E '\.(csv|jsonl)$'; cat ../../tests/test_fees.py; cat ../../tools/check_fees.py | head -60
cd /app; mkdir -p out; python3 bin/fees.py data out/statements.json && python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -20; python tools/check_fees.py
cd /app; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -5; python tools/check_fees.py; echo exit $?
